title: Стоп-лист и признание гостьи  (The Stop-List and the Guest's Confession)

segments.t: Escalating the feud with Vika, Chef Barinov forbids the waitresses from stepping past the kitchen line and places half the menu on the stop-list. Out in the dining room, Max apologizes to his older guest, who confesses that she actually comes to Claude Monet for a certain young man.
Вы знаете, Максим, я хочу вам признаться.
Вам, видимо, нравится, как я готовлю?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Ah, so that is how you want to play it, huh?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'oh' and finishing on 'yes'. Sasha answers right away.
'Now listen to my new order.' The grammar packs 'now' and 'order' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Entering is strictly forbidden.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'went in' and finishing on 'it is forbidden'.
'And just what are you going to do about it?' The grammar packs 'both' and 'will do' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
'What are you doing? Quiet down!' The meaning hinges on 'you' working together with 'easy' in spoken Russian.
'I was not the one who started this war.' Notice how Russian expresses 'not' and 'war' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Have you lost your minds completely?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'at all'. Sasha answers right away.
'Those items are on the stop-list.' In Russian, the idea of 'they' flows naturally into '86'd list' without extra filler words.
'That is quite alright, Maxim.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'nothing' before landing on 'Maxim'.
Вы знаете, Максим, я хочу вам признаться.
'You know, Maxim, I want to make a confession to you.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to admit', turning the action back on the subject. Max answers right away.
'Yes, I noticed that.' The meaning hinges on 'yes' working together with 'noticed' in spoken Russian.
Вам, видимо, нравится, как я готовлю?
'You apparently really like the way I cook?' Sasha anchors the line on 'for you', while 'prepare' completes the thought.
'I come here for the sake of one young man.' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'fellow' in spoken Russian. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Вы знаете, Максим, я хочу вам признаться.
Вам, видимо, нравится, как я готовлю?
